newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire Pacific says share price too low.
newsitem.headline: Swire Pacific says share price too low.

text.p: The "slightly lacklustre performance" of Swire Pacific Ltd's share price is undeserved, a senior company executive said on Friday.
Swire's share price has fallen 16.6 percent between the end of last year and March 14, while the Hang Seng Index was down just 5.3 percent over the same period.

"Our view is that the slightly lacklustre performance (of Swire's share price) is not deserved, and I feel that we will be able to demonstrate in the longer term that this is unjustified," finance director Peter Johansen said at a news conference on Swire's 1996 results.
Chairman Peter Sutch said the underperformance could possibly be blamed on nervousness over Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, a 43.86 percent associate of Swire, and on Swire's land acquisition plans.
"Talk of fuel prices, pressure on yields, weakness of the yen, I think, flowed through from the Cathay Pacific share price into the Swire Pacific one," Sutch said.
Another factor could be Swire's plans to replenish its land bank, said Sutch.
In a statement accompanying the 1996 results, Sutch said plans to add to Swire's land bank remained a "top priority".
